items.en: The World of Meaning: How the Body Came to Be
items.zh: 通明觀 · 義世間 · 根本世間因緣

zh: 第二、次釋約義世間明中次根行者，進證初禪五支之相，即為二：一者、正明義世間相；二者、即釋成覺義。就第一、釋義世間為二意：一、明外義世間；二、明內義世間。今釋外義世間，復為三意：一、正明根本世間因緣；二、明根本與外世界相關；三、明王道治正。
en: Second, next explaining, with reference to the world of meaning, how a practitioner of middle faculty progresses in realizing the mark of the first dhyāna's five factors: this itself has two parts — directly clarifying the mark of the world of meaning; and explaining how this constitutes the sense of initial thought.

As for the first, explaining the world of meaning: this has two parts — clarifying the external world of meaning; and clarifying the internal world of meaning. Here, explaining the external world of meaning: this, in turn, has three parts — directly clarifying the causes and conditions of the root world; clarifying how the root world is interrelated with the external world; and clarifying the royal way of governance.

zh: 第一、釋覺知根本世間因緣生義。行者初得初禪，既已證見根本世間，爾時或見道，或未見道。今欲深知此根本世間一期果報因何而生，爾時於三昧內心慧明利，諦觀身內三十六物、四大、五陰，以願知心，願知此身何因緣有。三昧、智慧、福德、善根力故，即便覺知，如是身命皆由先世五戒業力持於中陰，不斷不滅，於父母交會之時，業力變識，即計父母身分精血二渧，大如豆子，以為己有，識托其間，爾時即有身根、命根、識心具足。識在其間，具有五識之性，七日一變，如薄酪凝酥，於後漸大，如雞子黃。
en: First, explaining the sense of awakening to how the root world arises through its own causes and conditions. The practitioner, having just attained the first dhyāna and thereby already realized and seen the root world, may, at this point, either have seen the path or not yet have seen it. Wishing now to know deeply through what causes and conditions this root world's own present-life karmic result actually arises, one closely contemplates, at this point, within samādhi, with a bright and sharp mind, the body's own thirty-six substances, the four elements, and the five aggregates, wishing with the mind to know through what causes and conditions this very body came to exist.

Through the power of samādhi, wisdom, merit, and wholesome roots, one thereupon becomes aware directly: this very body and life are, in every case, sustained through the karmic power of the five precepts from a past life, carried through the intermediate state, neither cut off nor extinguished, and, at the very moment of the parents' union, this karmic power transforms consciousness, taking hold of a portion of the parents' own bodily essence — the two drops of semen and blood, the size of a bean — as one's own, consciousness lodging itself between them. At this point, the faculty of the body, the faculty of life, and the mind of consciousness are already complete. Consciousness, present between them, is already complete with the nature of the five sense-consciousnesses, transforming once every seven days, like thin whey or congealed cream, afterward growing gradually larger, like the yolk of a chicken's egg.

zh: 業力因緣，變此一身，內先為者，五臟安置五識，爾時即知不殺戒力變此身內次為肝臟，則魂依之；不盜戒力變此身內以為腎臟，則志依之；不婬戒力變此身內為肺臟，則魄依之；不妄語戒力變此身內以為脾臟，則意依之；不飲酒戒力即變身內以為心臟，則神依之。此魂、志、魄、意、神五神即是五識之異名也。
en: Through the causes and conditions of this karmic power, this single body is transformed: within it, first, the five internal organs are established, each housing one of the five consciousnesses. At this point, one comes to know directly: the power of the precept against killing transforms, within this body, what becomes the liver, upon which the "cloud-soul" depends; the power of the precept against stealing transforms, within this body, what becomes the kidneys, upon which the "will" depends; the power of the precept against sexual misconduct transforms, within this body, what becomes the lungs, upon which the "animal-soul" depends; the power of the precept against false speech transforms, within this body, what becomes the spleen, upon which "intention" depends; and the power of the precept against intoxicants transforms, within this body, what becomes the heart, upon which the "spirit" depends. These five, cloud-soul, will, animal-soul, intention, and spirit, are precisely alternate names for the five consciousnesses themselves.

zh: 五臟宮室既成，則神識則有所栖。既有栖託，便須資養。五戒業力復變身內以為六府神氣，府養五臟及與一身。府者，膽為肝府，盛水為氣，合潤於肝。小腸為心府，心赤，小腸亦赤，心為血氣，小腸亦通血氣，主潤於心，入一身故。大腸為肺府，肺白，大腸亦白，主殺物益肺，成化一身。胃為脾府，胃黃，脾亦黃，胃亦動作黃間，通理脾臟，氣入四支。膀胱為腎府，腎府黑，膀胱亦黑，通濕氣潤腎，利小行腸故。三焦合為一府分，各有所主。上焦主通津液清溫之氣，中焦主通血脈精神之氣，下焦主通大便之物。三焦主利上下五臟之神，分治六府，六府之氣以成五官之神，主治一身義。
en: The five organs, serving as their own palace-chambers, now complete, the spirit-consciousness thereby has a place to dwell. Having this dwelling, it must then be nourished and sustained. The karmic power of the five precepts further transforms, within the body, the six repositories' own spirit-energy, these repositories nourishing the five organs and the body as a whole.

As for these repositories: the gallbladder is the liver's own repository, holding fluid as its energy, jointly moistening the liver. The small intestine is the heart's own repository — the heart is red, and the small intestine, too, is red; the heart governs blood and energy, and the small intestine, too, circulates blood and energy, moistening the heart, entering the body as a whole. The large intestine is the lungs' own repository — the lungs are white, and the large intestine, too, is white; it governs the killing of things, benefiting the lungs, completing the body's own transformation. The stomach is the spleen's own repository — the stomach is yellow, and the spleen, too, is yellow; the stomach, too, moves and works within the yellow region, regulating the spleen, its energy entering the four limbs. The bladder is the kidneys' own repository — the kidneys' repository is black, and the bladder, too, is black; it circulates moisture, nourishing the kidneys, benefiting the lower intestine's own function. The triple burner combines to form a single repository, divided into parts, each governing its own function: the upper burner governs the circulation of bodily fluids and the clear, warm energy; the middle burner governs the circulation of blood, vessels, and vital energy; and the lower burner governs the circulation of solid waste. The triple burner governs the benefit of the five organs' own spirit, above and below, dividing to govern the six repositories, the six repositories' own energy thereby completing the spirit of the five faculties, governing the sense of the body as a single whole.

zh: 府臟相資，出生七體。腎生二體：一、骨；二、髓。腎屬於水，以水內有砂石故，即骨之義也。肝生二體：一、筋；二、腸。肝為木，木為地筋，故生筋、腸也。心生血脈，心色赤屬血，以通神氣，其道自然。脾生肌膚，脾為土，肌膚亦土。肺生於皮，肺在眾臟之上，故皮亦是一身之上。是為五臟能生七體，亦名七支。肺為大夫，在上下，捨不義。肝為尉。仁心在中央，稟種類。脾在其間，平五味。腎在下，衝四氣，增長七體成身。骨以柱之，髓以膏之，筋以縫之，脈以通之，血以潤之，肉以裹之，皮以覆之，以是因緣，則有頭、身、手、足大分之軀，餘骨為齒，餘肉為舌，餘筋為爪，餘血為髮，餘皮為耳。識神在內，戒力因緣，則五胞開張，四大造色清淨，變為五情，是以對塵則依情以識知，五色因緣則生意識，塵謝則識歸五臟。一期果報，四大、五陰、十二入、十八界具足成就。此則略說一期果報根本，世間義所因由。
en: The repositories and organs, mutually sustaining one another, give rise to the seven bodily constituents. The kidneys give rise to two: bones, and marrow — the kidneys belong to water, and, since water contains within it sand and stone, this is precisely the sense of bone. The liver gives rise to two: sinews, and intestines — the liver is wood, and wood is the earth's own sinew, hence it gives rise to sinews and intestines. The heart gives rise to blood and vessels — the heart's own color is red, belonging to blood, circulating the spirit's own energy, its course entirely natural. The spleen gives rise to flesh and skin's own surface — the spleen is earth, and flesh and skin's surface are earth as well. The lungs give rise to the skin — the lungs sit above the other organs, and so the skin, too, is the body's own uppermost layer. This, then, is how the five organs are able to give rise to the seven bodily constituents, also named the seven supports.

The lungs serve as the great minister, positioned above and below, setting aside what is unrighteous. The liver serves as the commandant. The benevolent heart resides at the very center, receiving the various kinds. The spleen resides between them, harmonizing the five flavors. The kidneys reside below, driving the four energies, causing the seven bodily constituents to grow and complete the body. Bone serves as its pillar; marrow, its ointment; sinew, its binding; vessels, its circulation; blood, its moistening; flesh, its wrapping; and skin, its covering — and, through these very causes and conditions, the great divisions of the body arise: head, torso, hands, and feet. The remainder of the bone becomes the teeth; the remainder of the flesh becomes the tongue; the remainder of the sinew becomes the nails; the remainder of the blood becomes the hair; and the remainder of the skin becomes the ears.

Consciousness and spirit, present within, through the causes and conditions of the precepts' own power, cause the five bodily orifices to open outward, the four elements' own produced form becoming pure, transformed into the five faculties of feeling — and so, in response to a sense-object, one knows it through this very faculty; through the causes and conditions of the five colors, mind-consciousness thereby arises; and, once the sense-object has passed, consciousness returns once more to the five organs. The body's own single-life karmic result, the four elements, the five aggregates, the twelve sense-bases, the eighteen elements, is thereby complete in full. This, in brief, describes the root cause of the single-life karmic result, the reason behind the world of meaning.

zh: 問曰：若言識從內出，在五根間識別五塵，與外道義有何異耶？答曰：如《淨名經》說：「不捨八邪而入八正。」亦云：「六十二見是如來種。」此言何謂？如是等義，皆出《提謂經》，明非人所作。若於此義不了，在下自當可見。
en: Question: if it is said that consciousness comes forth from within, present among the five faculties, distinguishing the five sense-objects, how does this differ from the non-Buddhist teaching's own view? Answer: as the Vimalakīrti Sūtra says: "Without relinquishing the eight deviant paths, one enters the eight correct ones." It also says: "The sixty-two views are themselves the very seed of the Tathāgata." What is meant by this? Such senses as these are all given in the Sūtra of Trapusa, clarifying that this is not the work of any person's own contrivance. Should this sense not be fully understood here, it will be seen for itself further below.

This embryological account extends the "kalala" conception narrative already given in fascicles 1 and 5 into far greater physiological detail — the two drops the size of a bean, the weekly transformations, likened to thin whey or congealed cream — and adds something genuinely distinctive: each of the five precepts is said to actively construct one of the five organs, moral discipline literally building the body from the moment of conception onward. The Vimalakīrti citation anticipating the objection "isn't this just the non-Buddhist doctrine of a soul?" is worth watching for as this section continues: the treatise is fully aware how close this material sails to a substantialist self, and flags in advance that it intends to thread that needle rather than having missed the problem.

items.en: The World of Meaning: The Body as Cosmos
items.zh: 通明觀 · 義世間 · 內世間與外國土相關

zh: 第二、釋內世間與外國土義相關相。行者三昧、智慧、願智之力諦觀身時，即知此身具彷天地一切法俗之事。所以者何？如此身相，頭圓象天，足方法地，內有空種，即是虛空。腹溫暖，法春夏，背剛強，法秋冬，四季體，法四時，大節十二，法十二月，小節三百六十，法三百六十日，鼻口出氣息，法山澤谿谷中之風氣，眼目法日月，眼開閉，法晝夜，髮法星辰，眉為北斗，脈為江河，骨為玉石，皮肉為地土，毛法叢林。
en: Second, explaining the mark of how the internal world is interrelated with the external land. The practitioner, through the power of samādhi, wisdom, and the wish-to-know, closely contemplating the body, thereby knows that this body is complete with, and corresponds to, every mundane and conventional matter of heaven and earth alike. Why is this?

As for this bodily mark: the head is round, resembling heaven; the feet are square, corresponding to earth; within, there is the space-element, which is precisely empty space itself. The belly is warm, corresponding to spring and summer; the back is firm and strong, corresponding to autumn and winter. The body's four-season constitution corresponds to the four times of the year; the twelve great joints correspond to the twelve months; the three hundred sixty small joints correspond to the three hundred sixty days. The breath issuing from the nose and mouth corresponds to the wind and energy found among mountains, marshes, valleys, and streams. The eyes correspond to the sun and moon; the eyes opening and closing correspond to day and night. The hair corresponds to the stars; the eyebrows are the Northern Dipper; the vessels are the rivers; the bones are jade and stone; the skin and flesh are the earth and soil; and the body-hair corresponds to forests and groves.

zh: 五臟在內，在天法五星，在地法五岳，在陰陽法五行，在世間法五諦。內為五神，修為五德，使者為八卦，治罪為五刑，主領為五官，昇為五雲，化為五龍。心為朱雀，腎為玄武，肝為青龍，肺為白虎，脾為勾陳。此五種眾生，則攝一切世間禽獸悉在其內。亦為五姓，謂宮、商、角、徵、羽，一切萬姓並在其內。對書典則為五經，一切書史並從此出。若對工巧，即是五明、六藝，一切技術悉出其間。當知此身雖小，義與天地相關。如是說身，非但直是五陰世間，亦是國土世間。
en: The five organs, present within, correspond, in heaven, to the five planets; on earth, to the five sacred peaks; in yin and yang, to the five phases; and, within the mundane world, to the five truths. Inwardly, they are the five spirits; cultivated, they are the five virtues; their messengers are the eight trigrams; their governance of transgression is the five punishments; their governing officials are the five offices; ascending, they are the five clouds; and, transformed, they are the five dragons. The heart is the Vermilion Bird; the kidneys are the Dark Warrior; the liver is the Azure Dragon; the lungs are the White Tiger; and the spleen is Gouchen, the Curved Array. These five kinds of beings thereby encompass every mundane bird and beast whatsoever, all contained within them.

They also correspond to the five clan-names — gong, shang, jiao, zhi, and yu — every family name in the ten thousand whatsoever contained within them as well. Matched against the classic texts, they are the five classics, every book and history whatsoever issuing forth from them. Matched against craft and skill, they are the five sciences and the six arts, every technique and skill whatsoever emerging from between them. One should know, then, that although this body is small, its own sense is interrelated with heaven and earth alike. Speaking of the body in this way, it is thus not merely the world of the five aggregates alone, but the world of the land itself as well.

This passage is unlike anything else in this treatise, and worth naming plainly: although the text itself attributes these correspondences to the Sūtra of Trapusa (提謂經), its content is indigenous Chinese cosmology rather than Indian Buddhist source material — the five phases (wood, fire, earth, metal, water), the eight trigrams of the Yijing, the four directional guardian creatures (Vermilion Bird, Dark Warrior, Azure Dragon, White Tiger), and the body-as-microcosm tradition of correlative cosmology already well established in Han-dynasty thought. Zhiyi's own sixth-century Chinese audience would have recognized this whole framework immediately, in a way no Indian source text would supply — a striking instance of a Buddhist meditation manual absorbing the surrounding culture's own cosmological vocabulary wholesale, presented here exactly as the source gives it, correspondence for correspondence, without softening how far it strays from anything Indian Buddhism itself would recognize as its own.

quiz.q: For practitioners of what faculty is the world of meaning explained?
quiz.why: The world of meaning is for practitioners of middle faculty; the root world is for the lower and the world of phenomena for the upper.

quiz.q: Which pairing of the five precepts with the five organs is correct?
options: not killing: liver; not stealing: kidneys; no misconduct: lungs; no false speech: spleen; no intoxicants: heart
quiz.why: Not killing forms the liver (cloud-soul), not stealing the kidneys (will), no sexual misconduct the lungs (animal-soul), no false speech the spleen (intention), no intoxicants the heart (spirit).

quiz.q: Of what are the five spirits other names?
quiz.why: Cloud-soul, will, animal-soul, intention, and spirit are other names for the five consciousnesses.

quiz.q: Which pairing of repositories and organs is correct?
options: gallbladder–liver, small intestine–heart, large intestine–lungs, stomach–spleen, bladder–kidneys, with the triple burner
quiz.why: The gallbladder serves the liver, small intestine the heart, large intestine the lungs, stomach the spleen, bladder the kidneys, and the triple burner forms one more.

quiz.q: The five organs give rise to seven constituents. Which is correct?
options: kidneys: bone and marrow; liver: sinew and intestine; heart: blood and vessels; spleen: flesh; lungs: skin
quiz.why: Kidneys give rise to bone and marrow, liver to sinew and intestine, heart to blood and vessels, spleen to flesh, and lungs to skin.

quiz.q: Which statement about the "remainders" is correct?
options: remaining bone: teeth; flesh: tongue; sinew: nails; blood: hair; skin: ears
quiz.why: The remainder of bone becomes teeth, of flesh the tongue, of sinew the nails, of blood the hair, of skin the ears.

quiz.q: Asked how consciousness issuing from within differs from non-Buddhist views, how does the text answer?
options: citing the Vimalakīrti and saying these senses come from the Trapusa Sūtra, not human contrivance
quiz.why: It cites the Vimalakīrti Sūtra on entering the eight right paths without leaving the eight wrong ones, and says these senses all come from the Trapusa Sūtra, not from anyone's contrivance.

quiz.q: Which correspondence of the body to heaven and earth is correct?
options: round head: heaven; square feet: earth; twelve joints: months; 360 joints: days; eyes: sun and moon
quiz.why: The round head resembles heaven, square feet earth; twelve great joints the months, 360 small joints the days; eyes the sun and moon; hair the stars.

quiz.q: The text concludes the body is not merely the world of the five aggregates but also what?
quiz.why: Small as it is, the body's sense relates to heaven and earth; it is not only the world of the five aggregates but also the world of the land.

quiz.q: Which matching of organs to the spirit-animals is correct?
options: heart: Vermilion Bird; kidneys: Dark Warrior; liver: Azure Dragon; lungs: White Tiger; spleen: Gouchen
quiz.why: The heart is the Vermilion Bird, kidneys the Dark Warrior, liver the Azure Dragon, lungs the White Tiger, spleen Gouchen; these five encompass all birds and beasts.
